title: mcpx(testsupport): MCPX_TEST_REQUIRE has two divergent parsers, and CI's python3 entry is enforced by nothing

body:
## Finding

`MCPX_TEST_REQUIRE` is parsed by two divergent parsers in the same `testsupport` package, and CI's list contains an entry nothing enforces. The two semantics disagree on case and on the wildcard/labels, and the `python3` entry in CI's list has no consumer — both recreate the silently-green hole the mechanism exists to close.

## Evidence

- Source PRs: #3696 (merged, merge `d55d6c90a5c7a584140ebbe0a299bdde25c882a1`) added `pkgs/mcpx/internal/testsupport/require.go`; #3704 (merged, merge `855372038be7b060a39a6fbecb4f405a454ff112`) added `realRequired()` in `pkgs/mcpx/internal/testsupport/realserver.go`. One finding for the set: same variable, same package, two PRs in the same batch.
- On current main (`4cd2927643453bee47a0f764de534e229220cf88`, verified twice via the contents API):
  - `require.go` `RequiredBinaries()` (line 21) normalises entries with `strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(name))` and knows only exact binary names.
  - `realserver.go` `realRequired()` (line 64) does `strings.TrimSpace(entry)` with **no lower-casing**, and additionally honours `"realsoftware"`, `"real"`, and `"*"`.
  - So `MCPX_TEST_REQUIRE=RealSoftware` (or `REALSOFTWARE`) fails a missing *runtime binary* test via the first parser but only *skips* a missing real server via the second; `MCPX_TEST_REQUIRE=*` demands every real server but no runtime binary.
  - `.github/workflows/mcpx.yml` line 178 sets `MCPX_TEST_REQUIRE: deno,bun,node,python3`, but no call site passes `python3` to `RequireBinary`/`MissingRequired` (the e2e and probe call sites cover only deno/bun/node), and there is no suite-level check that every entry in `RequiredBinaries()` is present on PATH. Enforcement is purely per-test: an entry with no (or a `-run`-filtered-out) consumer silently does nothing.

## Why it matters

The require-list is a contract between CI configuration and the test suite. Two parsers drifting in the same package guarantee the contract means different things for runtimes and for real servers, and an unenforced entry makes CI claim a guarantee it does not check — the exact failure #1983 was filed to eliminate.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] One shared parser for `MCPX_TEST_REQUIRE` lives in `require.go` (with the label/wildcard rules stated once), and `realRequired` uses it.
- [ ] Case handling is identical for runtime binaries and real servers (a test pins `RealSoftware`/`REALSOFTWARE` behaviour).
- [ ] Either a suite-level enforcement fails CI when any listed entry is missing from PATH (covering `python3`), or `python3` is removed from the workflow list with the reason recorded.
- [ ] Existing testsupport tests still pass.
